newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK JAN-AUG TRADE DEFICIT WIDENS TO 35BLN - TASR.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK JAN-AUG TRADE DEFICIT WIDENS TO 35BLN - TASR.

text.p: The Slovak foreign trade deficit for the first eight months of the year widened to some 35 billion crowns from 31.9 billion in January-July period, the official TASR news agency reported on Thursday.

"The Slovak foreign trade deficit has been widening in the past two months by around three billion crowns, from 27 billion crowns in June, to about 32 billion in July and around 35 billion crowns in August," TASR quoted Stefan Burda, director of trade department at the economics ministry as saying.
Burda did not give further details on the trade figures and ministry officials were not immediatelly available for comment.
Earlier this month the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said it had revised its original forecast for a full year trade deficit, to 40-55 billion crowns.

The original NBS forecast for the 1996 foreign trade balance, made at the beginning of the year, was for a deficit of some 11 billion crowns. In 1995 Slovakia posted a foreign trade surplus of 1.8 billion crowns.

Government officials have said the turnabout was no cause for concern, as imports, totalling 182.13 billion crowns in January-July period, included oil, technology and investment goods needed to restructure the country's economy.
